subject: Post-demo: networking, control-plane isolation & validation plan
messages_1_subject: Post-demo: networking, control-plane isolation & validation plan
messages_1_body:
Thanks again for your time today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment:

Summary from call:
- FinStack is evaluating private deployments for PII-sensitive inference workloads (banking data). Primary concerns: control-plane egress, ability to run an air-gapped on-prem bundle, and deterministic failover to managed endpoints.
- Competitive lens: you are comparing Redwood private deployment vs HypCloud managed endpoints + self-hosted LLMs. You want a test plan to validate networking boundaries and fallback behavior.

Key Redwood differentiators we covered (high-level):
- Private deployment (VPC or on-prem) ships the control plane components to your environment; customers can opt for fully customer-controlled control plane with zero egress to Redwood-managed services.
- Our runtime supports same API surface across hosted and private modes, so your app logic and routing policies remain unchanged during failover tests.
- Built-in batch/caching knobs and KV-cache escape hatches that reduce token costs without changing quality profiles vs hyperscaler endpoints.

Proposed validation tests (we recommend running in this order):
1) Control-plane egress verification: validate that our private control plane establishes connections to the minimal set of Redwood endpoints (or zero if you pick customer-managed control-plane). We will provide IP ranges, FQDNs, and a handshake spec.
2) Latency baseline vs HypCloud: run a synthetic 1k token generation workload from your subnet to both HypCloud and Redwood private endpoint (same model family) to compare P50/P95 under identical concurrency.
3) Failover/fallback test: simulate a control-plane outage and validate application behavior when requests are routed to a managed fallback (if you enable it) or blocked (if strict isolation).
4) Air-gap feasibility review: for fully air-gapped installs we will provide our on-prem bundle checklist and a timeline for an offline install.

Requested items from FinStack to proceed:
- Confirm SecOps contact (you mentioned M. Chen).
- Which VPC region and whether there is a strict no-egress requirement for the control plane.
- A 2-week POC window in June where engineering can run the baseline tests.

I attached the private networking checklist and the annotated diagram from today’s demo. Karthik and Laura are looped for the technical plan and timeline. If this looks good I’ll circulate a Mutual Action Plan and proposed test commands by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
--

messages_3_subject: Re: Post-demo: networking, control-plane isolation & validation plan — technical details
messages_3_body:
Hi Anna / Ming (cc Rafael, Laura) — following up with the technical specifics you asked for and the handshake spec attached. Highlights below and the attached controlplane-handshake-spec.md has the full test commands and sample iptables rules.

Minimal connectivity options (customer-managed control plane):
- Option A (Zero egress): Fully customer-managed control plane (air-gapped). No outbound connections to Redwood required after initial bundle delivery. Requires offline transfer of bundle and an engineer to run the installer (we provide signed binaries).
- Option B (Restricted egress): Customer-managed control plane with limited outbound to a small set of Redwood validation endpoints. Ports: 443 outbound to 3 IP ranges for signing/health-checks. See list in the attached spec.

Egress IP ranges (sample):
- 34.120.10.0/24
- 34.120.11.0/24
(This list is for validation only; exact ranges change by release and will be in the spec.)

Test commands and expected signals:
- TLS handshake verification (curl with --resolve for host override).
- Simulated control-plane outage: drop egress to Redwood endpoints and verify routing rules fall back to a pinned model variant (or block if you choose strict isolation). We provide a small harness to run this without affecting production.

Hyperscaler comparison notes:
- HypCloud managed endpoints will have simpler network setup but cannot give you the zero-egress guarantee unless you self-host entirely; that means you’ll be responsible for orchestration, KV cache handling, and model updates.
- For latency parity we recommend the synthetic 1k token test with 8 concurrent streams; our team will provide the harness and the exact request traces to run side-by-side.

Attached: controlplane-handshake-spec.md (contains iptables examples, sample test harness commands, and expected logs). I’ll schedule a short 45-minute tech sync with Ming if that helps.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
